I checked the actual supplied immutable H0N return/Result/accepted-review responses at 51b980512a901f6aaa377c2805be24b1a0c6ebe1 against the ledger pins. With J0(x,y)=(ix,-iy), holomorphic coordinates (z,w)=(x,conjugate(y)) give E^3 x E^3 and holomorphic K action (a+bi,a-bi) on the two blocks. The displayed Riemann form is positive/integral with weights (1,1,1,1,1,3); the third weight cannot be replaced by 1. The diagonal is algebraic but need not be K-stable. This gives the stated special member of the same Hermitian carrier, rather than a claim on every or a very-general member.

I checked the two pure embedding terms in the graph cycle. In the stated determinant orders, the sigma coefficient is (i/2)^3: the three selected minus signs cancel the three interleaving swaps. The conjugate ordered coefficient has the opposite sign. The accepted projector acts as identity on these distinct pure lines and kills the other embedding counts, so their displayed nonzero difference is valid. Rationality follows from the rational cycle and projector; no independent reclassification of H0N is needed.

The global point-divisor Koszul calculation is sufficient for ch(O_Z)=[Z]: each of the three divisor squares is zero. A composition series of any finite O_D gives ch(O_D)=length(D)[point], concentrated in codimension six. Hence ch3(F_D)=[Z] for every such D. ## Nine directions and the geometric bridge to complete obstruction

K preservation forces the off-diagonal Beltrami blocks. Polarization with A=diag(I3,D0), D0=diag(1,1,3), imposes AC=(AC)^T and thus C(B)=[[0,B],[D0^-1 B^T,0]], with every B entry free. Restricting to the diagonal and applying q(vz,vw)=vw-vz gives delta(B)=D0^-1 B^T-B. This supplies all nine polarized K-linear directions. The two weighted 2-by-2 blocks have determinant 2/3, the (12,21) block has rank one, and the 33 coefficient is -2/3: rank six and the stated three-dimensional kernel follow on paper.

The finite-support lemma provides the essential extra argument; the normal matrix alone would be insufficient. I checked each direction of the following implication chain.

1. If a perfect lifting has derived special fibre F_D concentrated in degree zero, tensoring the dual-number exact sequence with it yields a degree-zero sheaf and an extension of F_D by F_D. Multiplication by epsilon is quotient followed by inclusion, so kernel equals image and the sheaf is R-flat. This avoids assuming flatness of a purported derived lift.
2. Away from Supp(D), the special fibre is O_Z. Local lifted generators make the lifted sheaf cyclic; their common annihilator is intrinsic and glues. Locally the quotient by that annihilator is the R-flat lifted sheaf, so it defines an embedded flat deformation of punctured Z. The restricted normal obstruction therefore vanishes.
3. At the finite punctures, smooth dimension at least three and local freeness of N give depth at least three. Local cohomology in degrees 1 and 2 vanishes, and localization makes H1(Z,N) -> H1(Z minus Supp(D),N) an isomorphism. The original normal obstruction vanishes. No length or reducedness assumption entered.
4. Conversely, zero normal Cech class glues an embedded first-order Z_R. A smooth affine open containing the finite support has affine nilpotent thickening and a noncanonical R-product trivialization, obtained from formal smoothness and R-flatness. The constant D_R is closed in Z_R (equivalently its finite proper map into separated Z_R is closed). Its ideal is R-flat and locally perfect; the regular closed immersion pushes it to a perfect lifting on X_R.

I independently opened Huybrechts--Thomas arXiv:0805.3527v2, introduction p.2 and Corollary 3.4 p.14, and checked the three cited Stacks tags. The import concerns the full truncated Atiyah/Kodaira--Spencer product and perfect-lift equivalence, without a simplicity, stability or Chern-trace replacement. Here the smooth special fibre makes F_D perfect, the square-zero ideal is O_X, and a projective first-order deformation embeds through P^m_R into the smooth complex ambient P^m_C x A^1_C. These match the required hypotheses. The companion PRIMARY_SOURCE_CHECKS.json records exact URLs/locators and paraphrased scope, without copying an external paper.

Consequently ker(Omega_D)=ker(delta) is justified for each D. This is the complete object obstruction, not its Chern-character trace; no semiregularity injectivity is assumed.

## Exact image matrix and independent bounded verification

For each fixed D, equal kernels give the unique injective map f_D:im(delta) -> Ext2(F_D,F_D) by f_D(delta(v))=Omega_D(v). The six normal columns (12,13,23,31,32,33) are independent, so their Yoneda images eta_ij(D) form a basis of im(Omega_D). The other kernel relations give exactly Q(B)=(B12-B21,B13,B23,B31,B32,B33). This validates the complete restricted 6-by-9 matrix in that D-dependent image basis. It does not identify entire Ext groups, canonical ambient Ext bases, or targets for different D. The uniform quantifier over D comes from the geometric lemma, not matrix enumeration.

"""One bounded independent exact check of the fixed H0P matrix input.

This task-specific verifier reuses SymPy Rational/Matrix. It imports no author
script, executes no scientific backend run, searches for no object, and proves
no geometric perfect-lift or Atiyah-obstruction identification.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
from pathlib import Path

import sympy as sp

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[5]
OUT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
READBACK = ROOT / 'research_notes/owner_goal_20261015/h0p_review_readiness/AUTHOR_PROOF_COPY_ACTUAL_READBACK.json'
SOURCE_COMMIT = '2edb5a7c55508c8e946d3012da1b954f81c127a9'
SOURCE_PATH = 'research_notes/owner_goal_20261015/HODGE_H0P_FROZEN_AUTHOR_PROOF_COPY_BUNDLE.json'
SOURCE_SHA256 = 'da3bc29a9bbf0e497fdfa0ccc15602fdea6c416f32e2e93768aec0095a24be03'
SOURCE_BLOB = '395ab7432740964921aeea7512f5adc297237010'


def sha256(data: bytes) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()


def blob_sha(data: bytes) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha1(b'blob ' + str(len(data)).encode() + b'\0' + data).hexdigest()


def rational_matrix(rows):
    return sp.Matrix([[sp.Rational(x) for x in row] for row in rows])


def encoded(matrix):
    return [[str(x) for x in row] for row in matrix.tolist()]


def row_vector(matrix):
    return sp.Matrix(list(matrix))  # SymPy's list(Matrix) is row-major.


def run():
    raw = READBACK.read_bytes()
    actual = json.loads(raw)
    assert actual.get('isError') is False
    content = actual['structuredContent']['content'].encode('utf-8')
    assert len(content) == 69171
    assert sha256(content) == SOURCE_SHA256
    assert blob_sha(content) == SOURCE_BLOB == actual['structuredContent']['sha']
    assert actual['structuredContent']['display_url'] == (
        f'https://github.com/awdawmip/enterprise-math/blob/{SOURCE_COMMIT}/{SOURCE_PATH}')
    bundle = json.loads(content)
    assert len(bundle['members']) == 8
    member_pins = []
    for member in bundle['members']:
        data = member['content'].encode('utf-8')
        assert len(data) == member['utf8_bytes']
        assert sha256(data) == member['sha256']
        if member.get('git_blob_sha1'):
            assert blob_sha(data) == member['git_blob_sha1']
        member_pins.append({
            'original_author_output_path': member['original_author_output_path'],
            'utf8_bytes': len(data), 'sha256': sha256(data), 'git_blob_sha1': blob_sha(data)})
    matrix_member = next(m for m in bundle['members']
                         if m['original_author_output_path'].endswith('/matrix_support/MATRICES.json'))
    matrices = json.loads(matrix_member['content'])
    assert matrices['external_model']['h_diagonal'] == [1, 1, 1, -1, -1, -3]
    assert matrices['external_model']['D_diagonal'] == [1, 1, 3]
    assert matrices['external_model']['polarization_weight_diagonal'] == [1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 3]
    order = ['11', '12', '13', '21', '22', '23', '31', '32', '33']
    assert matrices['conventions']['source_B_basis_order'] == order
    D = sp.diag(1, 1, 3)
    A = sp.diag(1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 3)
    H = sp.diag(1, 1, 1, -1, -1, -1)  # i eigenvalue signs; conjugation reverses them.
    z = sp.zeros(3)
    expected_tangents = []
    normal_columns = []
    basis = matrices['polarized_K_linear_tangent']['basis']
    assert len(basis) == 9
    for k, (i, j) in enumerate((i, j) for i in range(3) for j in range(3)):
        B = sp.zeros(3)
        B[i, j] = 1
        L = D.inv() * B.T
        C = z.row_join(B).col_join(L.row_join(z))
        assert basis[k]['label'] == 'kappa_' + order[k]
        assert rational_matrix(basis[k]['C_matrix']) == C
        assert H * C + C * H == sp.zeros(6)
        assert A * C == (A * C).T
        expected_tangents.append(row_vector(C))
        # q(vz,vw)=vw-vz and restriction dbar(z)=dbar(w)=dbar(t).
        normal_columns.append(row_vector(L - B))
    tangent_inclusion = sp.Matrix.hstack(*expected_tangents)
    assert tangent_inclusion.rank() == 9
    c = sp.Matrix(6, 6, sp.symbols('c0:36'))
    constraints = row_vector(H*c+c*H).col_join(row_vector(A*c-(A*c).T))
    coefficient_matrix, rhs = sp.linear_eq_to_matrix(list(constraints), list(c))
    assert rhs == sp.zeros(72, 1)
    assert coefficient_matrix.rank() == 27
    assert coefficient_matrix * tangent_inclusion == sp.zeros(72, 9)
    M = sp.Matrix.hstack(*normal_columns)
    assert M == rational_matrix(matrices['normal_support_obstruction']['matrix'])
    assert M.rank() == 6
    K = rational_matrix(matrices['normal_support_obstruction']['kernel_inclusion_9_by_3'])
    assert K.rank() == 3 and M*K == sp.zeros(9, 3)
    computed_kernel = sp.Matrix.hstack(*M.nullspace())
    assert K.row_join(computed_kernel).rank() == 3
    rref, pivots = M.rref()
    eta_columns = [1, 2, 5, 6, 7, 8]  # 12,13,23,31,32,33
    J = M[:, eta_columns]
    assert J.rank() == 6
    minor_rows = [1, 2, 5, 6, 7, 8]
    minor = J[minor_rows, :]
    assert minor.det() != 0
    Q = sp.zeros(6, 9)
    Q[0, 1], Q[0, 3] = 1, -1
    for r, col in enumerate([2, 5, 6, 7, 8], start=1):
        Q[r, col] = 1
    assert M == J*Q and Q.rank() == 6 and Q*K == sp.zeros(6, 3)
    assert sp.Matrix.hstack(*Q.nullspace()).row_join(K).rank() == 3
    assert M[:, 3] == -M[:, 1]
    assert M[:, 0] == M[:, 4] == sp.zeros(9, 1)
    assert M[:, 8] == sp.Matrix([0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0,sp.Rational(-2,3)])
    output = {
        'schema': 'H0P_FIXED_INPUT_INDEPENDENT_LINEAR_CHECK_V1',
        'classification': 'AUXILIARY_NONBLIND_SCIENTIFIC_PRELIMINARY_NOT_NATIVE_VOTE',
        'reviewer_id': 'EM-DIRECT-595FEB',
        'activity_id': 'RA-95FA5339F77A27044B340F0B',
        'runtime': {'python_library': 'sympy', 'sympy_version': sp.__version__,
                    'arithmetic': 'exact Rational; no floating point'},
        'source': {'repository': 'awdawmip/enterprise-math', 'commit': SOURCE_COMMIT,
                   'path': SOURCE_PATH, 'utf8_bytes': len(content),
                   'sha256': sha256(content), 'git_blob_sha1': blob_sha(content),
                   'actual_readback_local_path': str(READBACK),
                   'actual_readback_file_sha256': sha256(raw)},
        'all_eight_member_pins': member_pins,
        'verified': {
            'all_member_sizes_hashes_and_available_blob_pins_match': True,
            'all_nine_transcribed_6_by_6_C_matrices_match_formula': True,
            'K_and_polarization_constraint_rank_on_36_variables': 27,
            'complete_tangent_dimension': 9,
            'all_81_normal_entries_match_independent_restriction_quotient_formula': True,
            'normal_rank': 6, 'kernel_dimension': 3,
            'kernel_inclusion_full_rank_and_spans_exact_nullspace': True,
            'six_eta_direction_normal_images_independent': True,
            'normal_map_factors_as_J_times_Q': True,
            'quotient_matrix_Q_rank': 6, 'Q_and_normal_map_same_kernel': True},
        'certificates': {'normal_matrix': encoded(M), 'rref': encoded(rref),
                         'rref_pivot_columns_zero_based': list(pivots),
                         'kernel_inclusion_in_author_basis_order': encoded(K),
                         'eta_source_labels': [order[k] for k in eta_columns],
                         'independent_image_columns_J': encoded(J),
                         'nonzero_6_by_6_minor_row_labels': [order[k] for k in minor_rows],
                         'nonzero_6_by_6_minor_determinant': str(minor.det()),
                         'quotient_image_coordinate_matrix_Q': encoded(Q)},
        'logical_boundary': [
            'Only the fixed first-order external carrier D=diag(1,1,3) is checked.',
            'No geometric lemma or full Ext/Atiyah obstruction is computed or proved by this check.',
            'For each finite D, if the primary reviewer establishes linear ker(Omega_D)=ker(delta_Z), then Omega_D factors uniquely through im(delta_Z) by an injective linear map.',
            'Under that same per-D hypothesis the six eta images form a basis of im(Omega_D), and Q is its coordinate matrix.',
            'Equal kernels identify image quotients, not entire Ext groups, canonical Ext bases, or different-D Ext targets.',
            'No Native execution, formal review vote, new task/claim/DA, author artifact mutation, old script rerun, object search or higher-order claim is made.']}
    (OUT/'EXACT_LINEAR_CHECK_RESULT.json').write_text(json.dumps(output,indent=2)+'\n')
    print(json.dumps({'status':'EXACT_FIXED_LINEAR_CHECK_PASSED',
                      'normal_rank':6,'kernel_dimension':3,
                      'independent_6_by_6_minor_determinant':str(minor.det()),
                      'result_path':str(OUT/'EXACT_LINEAR_CHECK_RESULT.json')},indent=2))


if __name__ == '__main__':
    run()
